correctness.rationale: From actual pinned RESULT.md: after zeros are omitted, f_l(x)=max_{1<=t<=s}S_t(x)/(l+t). The active full-support branch equals 1/(l+s) for sufficiently large l and telescopes the infinite defining series. For y=((1-e)x,e), e<=(1-e)min x, the new coordinate is last and f_l(y)=max((1-e)f_l(x),1/(l+s+1)); switching at l=M-s-1, M=floor(1/e), gives F(y)=(1-e)F(x)+e H_{M-1}+1/M with exact boundary ties. Symmetry and concavity of the original harmonic-entropy objective then imply maximum binary increment occurs from the boundary; formula valid to distance 1, and range F in [0,1] saturates for delta>=1. For d fixed, largest-partial-sum total-variation control |f_l(x)-f_l(y)|<=e/(l+1), uniform tail <=(d-1)/(L+1), choice L~(d-1)/e yields upper e log(1/e)+O_d(e). The embedded two-coordinate example attains it. Independent rational checker ran 2808 tests; these finite tests are corroboration, not the analytic argument.
